name: Iron deficiency anaemia
overview: Iron deficiency anaemia is when a lack of iron means the body cannot make enough healthy red blood cells. It is common and can make you feel tired and short of breath. It is usually easy to treat, but the cause should be found.
symptoms: Tiredness and lack of energy
Shortness of breath
Noticeable heartbeats (palpitations)
Pale skin
Headaches
Craving non-food items such as ice (pica)
causes: Heavy periods
Pregnancy
Bleeding in the gut, for example from ulcers or bowel cancer
Not enough iron in the diet
Conditions that stop the body absorbing iron, such as coeliac disease
riskFactors: Vegetarian or vegan diet without enough iron-rich foods
diagnosis: Anaemia is diagnosed with a blood test; further tests may be needed to find the cause of the iron deficiency.
treatment: Iron tablets or liquid prescribed by a doctor
Iron given into a vein in some cases
Treating the underlying cause, such as heavy periods or bleeding
selfCare: Eat iron-rich foods such as dark green leafy vegetables, beans, fortified cereals, meat and dried fruit
Avoid tea or coffee with meals, which can reduce iron absorption
whenToSeeDoctor: Symptoms of anaemia such as tiredness and breathlessness
Heavy periods
Symptoms not improving after treatment
emergencySigns: Vomiting blood or black, tarry stools

name: Hay fever
overview: Hay fever is an allergic reaction to pollen, usually worse between late March and September in temperate climates. It causes sneezing, a runny nose and itchy eyes. It cannot be cured, but symptoms can be eased with pharmacy treatments.
symptoms: Sneezing and coughing
Runny or blocked nose
Itchy, red or watery eyes
Itchy throat, mouth, nose and ears
Headache or tiredness
Loss of smell
causes: An allergic reaction to pollen from trees, grass or weeds
The immune system overreacting to a harmless substance
riskFactors: Living in areas with high pollen
diagnosis: Hay fever is usually diagnosed from symptoms and when they happen; allergy testing is rarely needed.
treatment: Antihistamine tablets, drops or nasal sprays
Immunotherapy for severe cases, under a specialist
selfCare: Put petroleum jelly around nostrils to trap pollen
Shower and change clothes after being outside
Keep windows and doors shut on high pollen days
prevention: Start treatment before the pollen season if advised
whenToSeeDoctor: Symptoms not improving with pharmacy medicines
Breathing problems such as wheezing or a tight chest
emergencySigns: Swelling of the lips, tongue or throat

name: Food allergy
overview: A food allergy is when the immune system reacts to a food as if it were harmful. Reactions can be mild or, sometimes, severe and life-threatening (anaphylaxis). Common triggers include peanuts, tree nuts, milk, eggs, fish, shellfish, wheat and sesame.
symptoms: Itching or tingling in the mouth
Itchy rash or hives
Swelling of the lips, face, tongue or throat
Sneezing, runny nose or itchy eyes
Tummy pain, feeling sick, vomiting or diarrhoea
Severe reactions: difficulty breathing, wheezing, dizziness or collapse
causes: The immune system wrongly reacting to proteins in certain foods
Common triggers include milk, eggs, peanuts, tree nuts, fish, shellfish, wheat, soya and sesame
diagnosis: A doctor or allergy specialist uses your history of reactions, skin prick tests, blood tests and sometimes supervised food challenges.
treatment: Adrenaline auto-injectors for people at risk of anaphylaxis
Specialist allergy care, sometimes including desensitisation treatment
selfCare: Tell restaurants and schools about the allergy
Carry prescribed adrenaline auto-injectors at all times if you have them
prevention: For babies, follow current advice on introducing allergenic foods; ask a health professional if your baby has eczema or a known allergy
whenToSeeDoctor: You or your child react after eating a food
Mild reactions that keep happening
emergencySigns: Swelling of the throat or tongue, or difficulty swallowing
Signs of anaphylaxis: use an adrenaline auto-injector if available and call emergency services

name: Anaphylaxis
overview: Anaphylaxis is a severe, life-threatening allergic reaction that happens very quickly. It is a medical emergency. Adrenaline is the main treatment and should be given straight away if available.
symptoms: Swelling of the throat and tongue
Difficulty breathing, wheezing or noisy breathing
Feeling lightheaded or faint
Tight throat or trouble swallowing
Skin that feels cold to the touch or a rash
Collapsing or losing consciousness
causes: Foods such as nuts, milk, fish, shellfish and eggs
Insect stings, such as wasp or bee stings
Some medicines, such as certain antibiotics
Latex
riskFactors: Known allergy to stings or medicines
diagnosis: Anaphylaxis is diagnosed from symptoms during the reaction; an allergy specialist then tests for the trigger.
treatment: Adrenaline injection straight away, using an auto-injector if available
Referral to an allergy specialist afterwards
selfCare: Use an adrenaline auto-injector if available; a second dose may be given after 5 minutes if no improvement
Lie down with legs raised, or sit up if breathing is difficult
Carry two auto-injectors at all times if prescribed
prevention: Carry prescribed adrenaline auto-injectors and know how to use them
whenToSeeDoctor: After any severe allergic reaction, for referral to an allergy specialist
If you have had a reaction and have not been tested
emergencySigns: Swelling of the throat or tongue

name: Lupus (SLE)
overview: Lupus is a long-term condition where the immune system attacks healthy tissue, causing inflammation in the joints, skin and other organs. Symptoms often come and go in flares. Treatment can control symptoms and protect organs.
symptoms: Joint and muscle pain
Extreme tiredness
Rashes, often across the cheeks and nose or on sun-exposed skin
High temperature
Hair loss and mouth ulcers
Swollen glands
causes: The immune system attacking the body's own tissues (an autoimmune condition)
A combination of genetic, hormonal and environmental factors such as sunlight or infections
riskFactors: Being of African, Caribbean, Asian or Hispanic descent
diagnosis: Lupus is diagnosed by a specialist using symptoms, examination and blood and urine tests, including antibody tests.
treatment: Antimalarial medicines used to treat lupus
Regular monitoring of kidneys and other organs
selfCare: Learn to spot signs of a flare
prevention: Sun protection and avoiding known triggers can reduce flares
whenToSeeDoctor: Ongoing joint pain, tiredness and rashes
Symptoms of a flare if you have lupus
Swelling of the legs or foamy urine
emergencySigns: High fever with feeling very unwell while on immune-suppressing medicines

name: Sickle cell disease
overview: Sickle cell disease is an inherited condition that affects red blood cells, making them an unusual shape. It can cause painful episodes, anaemia and a higher risk of infections. Treatment and care can help people live well.
symptoms: Painful episodes (sickle cell crises)
Tiredness and shortness of breath from anaemia
Increased risk of serious infections
Delayed growth in children
Yellowing of the skin or eyes
causes: An inherited change in the gene for haemoglobin
A child must inherit the gene from both parents to have the disease
riskFactors: Both parents carrying the sickle cell gene
Family origins in Africa, the Caribbean, the Middle East, India or the Mediterranean
diagnosis: Sickle cell disease is diagnosed with a blood test; many countries screen newborns and offer screening in pregnancy.
treatment: Antibiotics and vaccines to prevent infections
Blood transfusions, and stem cell or gene therapies for some people
selfCare: Keep up with vaccines and prescribed medicines
prevention: Carrier screening and genetic counselling for couples who may both carry the gene
whenToSeeDoctor: Pain not controlled at home
Signs of infection
Increasing tiredness or paleness
emergencySigns: Severe pain not relieved by usual medicine
Sudden weakness, confusion or problems speaking
A painful erection lasting more than 2 hours

name: Breast cancer
overview: Breast cancer is one of the most common cancers. It mostly affects women but can also affect men. Finding it early through screening and checking your breasts improves the chance of successful treatment.
symptoms: A new lump or thickening in the breast or armpit
A change in the size or shape of a breast
Skin changes such as dimpling, puckering or redness
Changes to the nipple, such as turning inwards
Discharge or bleeding from the nipple
A rash on or around the nipple
causes: Changes in breast cells that make them grow uncontrollably
Influenced by age, genes, hormones and lifestyle
riskFactors: Family history or inherited gene changes such as BRCA1 or BRCA2
diagnosis: Breast cancer is diagnosed with a breast examination, a mammogram or ultrasound, and a biopsy.
selfCare: Get to know how your breasts normally look and feel
whenToSeeDoctor: Any new lump or change in the breast or armpit
Nipple changes or discharge
Skin changes on the breast

name: Lung cancer
overview: Lung cancer is one of the most common and serious cancers. Smoking is the main cause, but people who have never smoked can also get it. It often has no symptoms early on, so getting persistent symptoms checked is important.
symptoms: A cough that lasts more than 3 weeks or changes
Chest infections that keep coming back
Coughing up blood
Pain when breathing or coughing
Persistent breathlessness
Tiredness and unexplained weight loss
causes: Smoking, the main cause
Exposure to second-hand smoke, radon gas, asbestos and air pollution
riskFactors: Smoking, now or in the past
Workplace exposure to asbestos and other chemicals
diagnosis: Lung cancer is diagnosed with a chest X-ray, CT scan and a biopsy; some countries offer lung screening for people at high risk.
selfCare: Stay active and eat well during treatment
prevention: Do not smoke and avoid second-hand smoke
Test your home for radon where advised
whenToSeeDoctor: A cough lasting more than 3 weeks
Coughing up blood
Unexplained breathlessness, weight loss or tiredness
emergencySigns: Coughing up a lot of blood
Sudden swelling of the face and neck

name: Bowel cancer
overview: Bowel cancer is cancer of the large bowel (colon) or back passage (rectum). It is one of the most common cancers. Screening can find it early or even prevent it by removing growths called polyps.
symptoms: Changes in your poo, such as looser poo, pooing more often or constipation
Blood in your poo or bleeding from the bottom
Needing to poo more or less often than usual
Tummy pain or a lump in the tummy
Bloating
Losing weight without trying and tiredness
causes: Changes in bowel cells, often starting in non-cancerous growths called polyps
Influenced by age, genes, diet and lifestyle
riskFactors: Diet high in red and processed meat and low in fibre
diagnosis: Bowel cancer is diagnosed with a stool test (FIT), a colonoscopy with biopsy, and scans.
prevention: Eat plenty of fibre and less red and processed meat
Do not smoke and limit alcohol
whenToSeeDoctor: Changes in bowel habits lasting 3 weeks or more
Blood in your poo
Unexplained weight loss or tiredness
A lump in your tummy
emergencySigns: Unable to poo or pass wind with a swollen tummy and vomiting

name: Prostate cancer
overview: Prostate cancer is one of the most common cancers in men. It often grows slowly and may not cause symptoms for many years. Some prostate cancers need treatment, while others can be safely monitored.
symptoms: Often no symptoms in early stages
Needing to pee more often, especially at night
Needing to rush to the toilet
Difficulty starting to pee or a weak flow
Feeling that the bladder has not emptied fully
Blood in urine or semen
causes: Changes in prostate cells
Influenced by age, genes and ethnicity
riskFactors: Family history of prostate or breast cancer
Inherited gene changes such as BRCA2
diagnosis: Prostate cancer is investigated with a PSA blood test, an examination, an MRI scan and a biopsy.
treatment: Hormone therapy and other medicines for advanced cancer
selfCare: Discuss the benefits and risks of PSA testing with a doctor
Stay active and keep to a healthy weight
prevention: There is no proven way to prevent prostate cancer; a healthy lifestyle is recommended
whenToSeeDoctor: Changes in how you pee
Blood in urine or semen
You are at higher risk and want to discuss testing
emergencySigns: New back pain with numbness or weakness in the legs, or loss of bladder or bowel control

name: Melanoma skin cancer
overview: Melanoma is a type of skin cancer that can spread to other parts of the body. It often appears as a new mole or a change in an existing mole. The main cause is ultraviolet light from the sun or sunbeds, and it is very treatable when found early.
symptoms: A new mole or a change in an existing mole
A mole with an uneven shape or border
A mole with several colours
A mole that is getting bigger
A mole that is itchy, crusting or bleeding
Can appear anywhere, including under nails and on the soles of the feet
causes: Damage to skin cells from ultraviolet (UV) light from the sun or sunbeds
Genetic factors
riskFactors: Lots of moles or unusual moles
History of sunburn or sunbed use
diagnosis: A doctor examines the skin and refers to a skin specialist, who may remove the mole for testing (biopsy).
treatment: Immunotherapy and targeted medicines for advanced melanoma
selfCare: Check your skin regularly for new or changing moles
prevention: Avoid sunburn: seek shade, cover up and use high-factor sunscreen
whenToSeeDoctor: A new mole or a change in an existing mole
A mole that is bleeding, itchy or crusting
A dark streak under a nail

sources.label: National Cancer Institute: Skin Cancer (Including Melanoma)

name: Non-melanoma skin cancer
overview: Non-melanoma skin cancers, mainly basal cell and squamous cell carcinomas, are the most common types of skin cancer. They usually develop on skin often exposed to the sun and are very treatable, especially when found early.
symptoms: A lump or discoloured patch on the skin that does not heal after 4 weeks
A scab or sore that keeps coming back
A shiny, pearly lump
A scaly, crusted patch that may bleed
Often on the face, ears, neck, lips, scalp or backs of the hands
causes: Long-term exposure to ultraviolet (UV) light from the sun or sunbeds, which damages skin cells
Less commonly, other factors such as previous radiotherapy or long-term immune suppression
riskFactors: Lots of sun exposure or sunbed use
A weakened immune system, for example after an organ transplant
diagnosis: A doctor examines the skin and may refer to a skin specialist for a biopsy.
treatment: Creams or freezing treatment for some early cancers
Radiotherapy or other treatments in some cases
selfCare: Protect your skin from the sun
prevention: Seek shade, cover up and use high-factor sunscreen
whenToSeeDoctor: A skin lump, patch or sore that has not healed after 4 weeks
A sore that keeps coming back or bleeding

sources.label: National Cancer Institute: Skin Cancer (Including Melanoma)

name: Cervical cancer
overview: Cervical cancer develops in the cervix, the entrance to the womb from the vagina. Almost all cases are caused by long-lasting infection with high-risk types of HPV. HPV vaccination and cervical screening can prevent most cases.
symptoms: Often no symptoms in early stages
Vaginal bleeding that is unusual, such as after sex, between periods or after menopause
Changes to vaginal discharge
Pain during sex
Pain in the lower back or pelvis
causes: Persistent infection with high-risk types of human papillomavirus (HPV)
Abnormal cell changes in the cervix that develop over years
riskFactors: A weakened immune system, such as with HIV
diagnosis: Cervical cancer is diagnosed through screening (HPV test), a colposcopy to look at the cervix, and a biopsy.
treatment: Treatment of abnormal cells before they become cancer
whenToSeeDoctor: Bleeding after sex, between periods or after menopause
Unusual vaginal discharge
Pain during sex
emergencySigns: Heavy vaginal bleeding that will not stop
